INTRO_KR: The HKSAR Government established the Hong Kong Council for Testing and Certification (HKCTC) in 2009 to advise it on the overall development strategy of the testing and certification industry. HKCTC comprises members from the industry, business sector and professional organisations as well as the relevant public bodies and Government departments. All members are appointed by the Chief Executive. The Innovation and Technology Commission provides secretariat and executive support to HKCTC. Having a robust accreditation system is also one of Hong Kong's key advantages in developing the testing and certification industry. Hong Kong Accreditation Service (HKAS) improves the standard of local conformity assessment services and supports the development of the industry by providing a wide range of accreditation services through three accreditation schemes, namely, the Hong Kong Laboratory Accreditation Scheme (HOKLAS); the Hong Kong Certification Body Accreditation Scheme (HKCAS); and the Hong Kong Inspection Body Accreditation Scheme (HKIAS).

INTRO_KR: Paul Fisher, Inc. was established in 1850 by Julius Fischer in Vienna, Austria, specializing in natural pearls. In the 1920s, Julius' grandson, Robert Fischer, expanded the company's offerings to include rare jewelry. Always maintaining a presence in Switzerland, Robert expanded to offices in London around 1938. The company relocated its headquarters to New York City in 1945 where it has flourished in the industry over 75 years. The New York years have been indelibly marked by Robert's son, Paul Fisher, an icon in the jewelry industry who passionately advocated for the future of the trade. Paul trained more than 40 international apprentices in the art of vintage and antique jewelry, emphasizing the importance of conducting business with the utmost integrity, leaving a lasting legacy that endures to this day. Today, Paul Fisher, Inc. is a globally recognized, sixth generation family jewelry business with a legacy of knowledge, integrity, and impeccable taste. With offices in New York, London, and Geneva, and a presence in Paris and Hong Kong, the company showcases their commitment to expanding their influence across the globe. They have built a sterling reputation for exceptional quality, honesty, and loyalty, and participate in numerous international shows and salons.

INTRO_KR: Jiabao Pavilion, a company that mainly focus on filigree inlay jewellery. Since its inception, with the attention to detail, exquisite craftsmanship and innovative spirit, it has created unique, fashionable and attractive filigree inlay jewellery. Filigree inlay, also known as fine gold art. Is a time-honored traditional Chinese handcraft art, which has a history of over 2000 years. In China and was once exclusively for the royal family. Filigree inlay, is famous for its sophisticated making procedure and precious raw materials, every procedure can further involve numerous tactics. In 2013, Peipei Liang, the founder of Jiabao Pavilion, was very fortunate to had met the filigree inlay artworks of the Ming and Qing dynasties in China at the British Museum in London, England. Miss. Liang was deeply attracted by those imposing artworks. After further study and understanding, Miss Liang determined to become the inheritor of filigree inlay. As a result, Jiabao Pavilion had successfully presented charming filigree inlay jewellery with delicate craftsmanship after establishment.

INTRO_KR: Alberto Vaccari (1933-2007) was from Valenza and he initially trained in Valenza as a model maker and goldsmith. This was before moving, while still very young, to Paris at the beginning of the 1950s, to learn the art of the Parisian jewellers (specialised in platinum and diamond jewellery), to broaden his knowledge of the sector and to develop an understanding of a more international taste. He returned to Valenza enriched by this unique experience, where he worked with other craftsmen and, towards the end of the 1970s, set up the Alberto Vaccari & C. In 1989, Alberto Vaccari and his son Manuel, ready for a new challenge, founded Ofir (with the AL3218 brand). The company was relocated to new premises in Corso Matteotti and production was totally renewed, thanks to the perfect professional and aesthetic understanding between father and son. After the death of his father in 2007, Manuel Vaccari continued his entrepreneurial career, taking care of the creative, production and commercial aspects of the business. His classic creations, though always with a modern edge and references to the world of design, are firmly rooted in the tradition of the highest Valenza craftsmanship, thanks to the skill of his craftsmen.

INTRO_KR: In 2019, Domenico Tavanti established the brand that still bears his name today. After decades of success in the goldsmithing industry, he fulfilled his dream of expressing his vision of luxury and beauty through a jewelry line that embodies the values of authenticity, beauty and craftsmanship. The Tavanti brand, born as a heartfelt tribute to his family, especially his wife and daughters, reflecting a deep and personal bond, has become a symbol of affection, care and timeless beauty. To bring this vision to life, Domenico entrusted the creative direction from the beginning to Fabrizio Falcinelli, a highly talented Tuscan jewelry designer whose distinctive approach enabled the development of collections blending innovation with tradition. He chose to enrich the brand's logo with a pair of dolphins, a pictogram symbolizing affection and love, reflecting Domenico's profound bond with his family. This visual choice, far from the usual commercial norms of the luxury industry, expresses the intimacy and warmth of family ties - core values of the brand. Wearing a Tavanti jewel today means embracing not just the elegance of an accessory, but carrying a fragment of Tuscan tradition, artisanal mastery and beauty rooted in the history of an Italian family.

The objective of Association is to promote the business development of Hong Kong's jewellery sector, uphold the goodwill of member companies, coordinate all member-to-member relationships, and harmonise industrial connections between the Association and other related organisations. It adopts the principle of fairness to resolve any disputes arisen. Member companies are also informed of Hong Kong's law and various regulations. When issues or incidents that hinder the industry's operation occur, the Association would write letters, submit articles or make use of other means to seek the government's resolution.
